content.title: About
content.content: Potato salad made with mayonnaise-type dressing is a popular dish consisting of boiled potatoes cut into cubes, mixed with mayo, mustard, vinegar, green onions, and sometimes additions such as eggs, pickles or ham.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato salad is a staple at picnics, barbecues and family celebrations.
In the United States the classic “Olivier” salad is considered a variation of potato salad with mayo.
Different countries use different dressings: Russia often uses sour cream, the US prefers mayo, Japan adds soy sauce and rice vinegar.
Traditionally the potatoes are boiled in their skins to help them keep their shape.
There is a “celery” version where a light yogurt dressing replaces mayonnaise.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The salad provides vitamins B6 and B9, important for metabolism and the nervous system.

items.title: Energy‑dense carbohydrates
items.content: Complex carbs in potatoes give sustained satiety.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Adding vegetables or herbs boosts fiber content, beneficial for digestion.

items.title: Healthy fats from mayo
items.content: Mayonnaise contains monounsaturated fats that, in moderation, can support heart health.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Mayonnaise makes the salad calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Traditional mayo contains eggs, which can trigger reactions in allergic individuals.

items.title: Bacterial growth risk
items.content: If left at room temperature for more than 2 hours, the salad can become a breeding ground for bacteria.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Pickles or store‑bought mayo can raise sodium content, which may be a concern for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve potato salad chilled as a side dish or a main course. Garnish with fresh herbs, paprika or sliced hard‑boiled eggs. It pairs well with grilled meats, fish or crusty bread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. Stir before serving to re‑incorporate the dressing. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or changes color.
